title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 6th Proof The Testimony Of The Purified Ones Scholars And Sages

questions.question: Who are described as giving united testimony in this passage?
questions.answer: Very large numbers of sincere, disciplined scholars and believing wise people who reached the highest levels of learning.

questions.question: Through whose teaching are these scholars and sages said to have reached their high rank?
questions.answer: Through the teaching and guidance of the Messenger described in the passage.

questions.question: What makes their achievement more striking according to the passage?
questions.answer: The one who taught them did not learn through ordinary reading and writing, yet he brought great knowledge and deep truths.

questions.question: What two major things do these scholars and sages unanimously confirm?
questions.answer: They confirm Allah’s oneness and also the truthfulness of the Messenger and the truth of what he said.

questions.question: How strong is their agreement presented to be?
questions.answer: It is presented as complete agreement supported by the strongest evidence.

questions.question: What is called the foundation of the Messenger’s mission in this passage?
questions.answer: Belief in the Divine unity of Allah.

questions.question: Besides proving Allah’s unity, what do these learned people testify about the Messenger himself?
questions.answer: They testify that he is a true teacher and that his message is trustworthy.

questions.question: Why does the passage call him a supreme teacher and great master?
questions.answer: Because his instruction raised countless scholars and sages to the highest level of learning and understanding.

questions.question: How is the proof in this passage described?
questions.answer: It is described as being as obvious and bright as daylight.

questions.question: What role does the Risale-i Nur have in this argument?
questions.answer: It is presented as one proof among the many proofs of his truthfulness.

questions.question: What does mentioning the many parts of the Risale-i Nur add to the point?
questions.answer: It strengthens the idea that there is extensive evidence supporting his truthfulness.

questions.question: What kind of people are highlighted at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: People of knowledge and wisdom who are sincere, careful, and spiritually refined.

questions.question: What level did they reach through the teachings mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They reached the highest degree of learning.

questions.question: What contrast does the passage draw about the teacher they followed?
questions.answer: It says he was not formally taught in the usual way, yet he brought extraordinary knowledge and truths.

questions.question: According to the passage, what did he bring that benefited these scholars and sages?
questions.answer: He brought sacred truths, high sciences, and God-given knowledge.

questions.question: What central belief do these scholars prove together?
questions.answer: They prove the oneness of Allah.

questions.question: Why is that central belief especially important in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it is described as the basis of his whole mission.

questions.question: What do they say about the one who taught these truths?
questions.answer: They bear united witness that he is truthful and reliable.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the truth of his words mean in simple terms?
questions.answer: It means what he said is accurate and deserving of belief.

questions.question: Is their witness shown as weak opinion or firm evidence? Explain.
questions.answer: It is shown as firm evidence because the passage says they agree unanimously and use the strongest proofs.

questions.question: What inference can be made from the fact that so many top scholars agree?
questions.answer: Their agreement adds serious weight and credibility to the claim that his message is true.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the clarity of this proof?
questions.answer: It says the proof is unmistakably clear, like broad daylight.

questions.question: How is the Risale-i Nur connected to the rest of the evidence?
questions.answer: It is included as a further proof supporting his truthfulness.

questions.question: What groups of learned people are mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Scholars and faithful sages.

questions.question: What qualities are attached to these people?
questions.answer: They are described as purified, sincere, careful, and highly trustworthy in their learning.

questions.question: How did they arrive at their advanced knowledge?
questions.answer: They reached it through the teachings and instruction found in the sacred truths brought by the Messenger.

questions.question: What is surprising about the source of these teachings?
questions.answer: The source is someone without formal literacy, yet he brought profound knowledge.

questions.question: What kinds of knowledge are connected to him in the passage?
questions.answer: Elevated sciences and knowledge given by Allah.

questions.question: What is the first truth these scholars and sages prove together?
questions.answer: Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What is the second truth they witness to together?
questions.answer: The truthfulness of the Messenger and the reliability of his speech.

questions.question: Why would their testimony matter so much in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: Because they are many in number, highly trained, and united in judgment.

questions.question: What comparison is used to explain the strength of this proof?
questions.answer: It is compared to the clarity of daylight.

questions.question: What example from later scholarship is named directly?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: Why is the Risale-i Nur mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: To show that even a large body of later work can serve as just one piece of evidence for his truthfulness.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the main claim about learned believers?
questions.answer: Their united judgment supports the truth of the Messenger’s mission.

questions.question: What kind of educational path led them to that judgment?
questions.answer: They were formed by the sacred teachings and truths that came through him.

questions.question: How does the passage present the teacher’s background in ordinary worldly learning?
questions.answer: It presents him as not having formal literacy in the usual sense.

questions.question: Even without that formal background, what did he contribute?
questions.answer: He brought lofty branches of knowledge and discovered Divine truths.

questions.question: What does this contrast help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps show that his knowledge could not be explained as ordinary human learning alone.

questions.question: What belief is named as the base of his mission?
questions.answer: The belief that Allah is One.

questions.question: How do the scholars and sages respond to that belief?
questions.answer: They confirm it together with very strong evidence.

questions.question: What else do they testify about beyond that belief?
questions.answer: They testify that the Messenger is truthful and that his statements are true.

questions.question: How does the passage emphasize the certainty of this proof?
questions.answer: By saying it is as plain and visible as daylight.

questions.question: What text is brought in as an added witness?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How should the mention of one hundred parts be understood in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows breadth and richness of evidence, even though all of it is treated as only one proof among many.

questions.question: What does the passage say happened to millions of scholars and sages through the Messenger’s teachings?
questions.answer: They rose to the highest rank of learning.

questions.question: What moral and intellectual qualities are attributed to these people?
questions.answer: They are presented as sincere, refined, exact, faithful, and wise.

questions.question: What source nourished their learning?
questions.answer: The sacred truths and instruction brought by the Messenger.

questions.question: Why does the passage point out that he was unlettered?
questions.answer: To highlight that such deep knowledge coming through him is extraordinary.

questions.question: What are the two kinds of knowledge or insight linked to him?
questions.answer: Advanced sciences and knowledge granted from Allah.

questions.question: What foundational truth do these learned people support?
questions.answer: The oneness of Allah.

questions.question: What do they say about the Messenger’s character and message?
questions.answer: They say he is truthful and that his words are true.

questions.question: How united are they in this testimony?
questions.answer: They are completely united in it.

questions.question: What kind of evidence do they use according to the passage?
questions.answer: The strongest kind of proofs.

questions.question: What conclusion can a reader draw from the scholars’ agreement and high status?
questions.answer: Their testimony is meant to be taken as powerful and dependable evidence.

questions.question: How does the passage help the reader picture the certainty of this evidence?
questions.answer: It compares it to something bright and obvious in daytime.

questions.question: In what way is the Risale-i Nur used in the final sentence?
questions.answer: It is presented as a supporting proof of the Messenger’s truthfulness.

questions.question: What broad category of people serves as evidence in this passage?
questions.answer: Highly learned and faithful people who became great scholars and sages.

questions.question: How many such people does the passage point to?
questions.answer: It points to millions of them.

questions.question: What does the passage say enabled them to reach such a high level?
questions.answer: The teachings and sacred truths brought by the Messenger.

questions.question: What unusual feature of the Messenger is stressed before mentioning the knowledge he brought?
questions.answer: His lack of ordinary literacy is stressed.

questions.question: What does the passage say he nevertheless brought forth or uncovered?
questions.answer: He brought elevated branches of knowledge and uncovered Divine knowledge.

questions.question: What first doctrine do these scholars establish together?
questions.answer: They establish Allah’s unity.

questions.question: How is that doctrine related to the Messenger’s mission?
questions.answer: It is the central base on which his mission stands.

questions.question: After that, what testimony do they give concerning the Messenger?
questions.answer: They testify that he is fully truthful and that his speech is true.

questions.question: What wording in the passage shows that their testimony is collective rather than individual?
questions.answer: It says they bear witness in complete agreement.

questions.question: What wording shows the quality of the evidence they use?
questions.answer: It says their evidence is of the strongest kind.

questions.question: What image is used to express how clear this proof is?
questions.answer: The image of bright daylight.

questions.question: Why is the Risale-i Nur mentioned even after all the other evidence?
questions.answer: To add one more concrete example showing that later works also point to the Messenger’s truthfulness.
